panels.title: How to read this dashboard
panels.description: Reading guide for this dashboard (added by the lab).

options.content:
Upstream **Calico Typha** dashboard (Calico v3.33.0). Typha is a fan-out cache between the Kubernetes API and every calico-node:
Felix watches Typha instead of the API server. With one node there are a few clients (syncers felix, node-status, tunnel-ip-allocation).
Healthy: clients streaming ≥ 1 for syncer felix, client fall-behind and ping latency in milliseconds, few connections accepted after
startup. Details: `docs/dashboards/networking.md`.

panels.title: Datastore cache size
panels.description: Number of datastore keys Typha holds in its cache (typha_cache_size): everything Felix needs (pods, policies, nodes…). Grows with the cluster; sudden drops = Typha restarted or lost the datastore.

panels.title: CPU Usage
panels.description: CPU seconds per second used by the Typha process (process_cpu_seconds_total).

panels.title: Memory Usage
panels.description: Resident memory of the Typha process (process_resident_memory_bytes).

panels.title: Total connections accepted
panels.description: New client connections per second accepted by Typha (typha_connections_accepted). Spikes = Felix/clients reconnecting.

panels.title: Client connections actively streaming
panels.description: Clients currently receiving updates from Typha (typha_connections_streaming): here calico-node (syncers felix, node-status, tunnel-ip-allocation). 0 for felix fires alert CalicoTyphaNoStreamingClients.
Number of client connections dropped to rebalance load.
panels.title: Rebalanced client connenctions

panels.description:
This metric measures how far behind Typha's clients are at reading updates.
It goes up if the client is slow or if Typha is overloaded and it cannot keep up with writes to all its clients.
It is normal for this to spike when new clients connect, they must download and process the snapshot, during which time they get slightly behind.
panels.title: 99%ile Client fall-behind
99%ile write latency
panels.description: Time Typha needs to write updates to a client socket (typha_client_write_latency_secs). High = slow client or network.

This metric tracks how long it takes for Typha's clients to respond to pings over the Typha protocol.
An increase in this metric indicates that the clients, network or Typha are more heavily loaded.
panels.title: 99%ile client ping latency

panels.description:
Internally, Typha stores datastore changes as a series of blocks called breadcrumbs.
The default maximum size of a block is 100 so, if Typha is consistently generating size-100 blocks it may be overloaded.
panels.title: 99%ile Breadcrumb Size

panels.description:
Internally, Typha stores datastore changes as a series of blocks called "breadcrumbs".
Each client "follows the breadcrumbs" either by blocking and waiting or skipping straight to the next one (non-blocking) if it is already available.
As load on Typha increases, the ratio of skip ahead non-blocking reads increases.  If it approaches 100% then Typha may be overloaded (since clients only do non-blocking reads when they're behind).
panels.title: Non-blocking breadcrumb fraction

panels.description:
This panel shows the rate of updates from the datastore(s).
For example, updates to Pods/Nodes/Policies/etc.
panels.title: Datastore updates total

panels.description:
This panel shows the number of updates from the datastore that Typha detected were no-ops.
For example, an update to a Kubernetes Node resource that didn't touch any values that Calico cares about.
Such updates are not propagated to clients, saving resources.
panels.title: Datastore updates skipped as no-ops

panels.description: This panel shows the 99%ile time to stream the initial datastore snapshot to each clients.
panels.title: Median snapshot send time

panels.description:
After sending the snapshot to the client, Typha allows a grace period for the client to catch up to the most recent data.
This metric tracks how many clients required the grace period.
panels.title: Clients requiring grace period
Max snapshot size (raw)
panels.description: Largest datastore snapshot Typha sent to a (re)connecting client, uncompressed (typha_snapshot_raw_bytes).

panels.title: Max snapshot size (compressed)
panels.description: Same snapshot after compression (typha_snapshot_compressed_bytes): what actually crosses the wire on reconnect.

title: Calico Typha (official)
description: Official Calico Typha dashboard from Calico v3.33.0 (https://github.com/projectcalico/calico/blob/v3.33.0/manifests/grafana-dashboards.yaml, key typha-dashboard.json). Lab changes: datasource, job="calico-typha" on every query (upstream used job typha_metrics or none), [30s] rate windows → $__rate_interval (30s scrape), guide panel, annotations, missing descriptions.
